picks.reason: Argentina's midfield completion rates remain elite, allowing them to suffocate possession and dictate the tempo of the final in the post-Messi era.
France possesses the deepest, fittest squad in the tournament, with Mbappe and Dembele providing a clinical edge off the bench that most teams cannot match.
After the Nations League final, Spain demonstrated that their high-pressing, possession-heavy system now has the physicality and intelligence to close out tight games.
England's xG metrics for the last three qualifying cycles are the highest in the world, suggesting their goal-scoring volume will eventually outpace defensive lapses.
Brazil are the only side with the individual 1v1 talent to break a packed defense, and the tournament format favors their chaotic attacking style over pragmatic grinding.

debate.line: PHOENIX, your Argentina squad has defensive fragility that will be exposed in a physical knockout game.
France is too reliant on individual brilliance; Argentina's system smothered the 2022 champions, so they will do it again.
NEXUS, Spain's possession is pretty to watch but they lack the clinical killer instinct when the game gets tight.
VEGA, your Brazil argument ignores that their defense is often caught out on the counter-attack by teams with quick transitions.
ORION, England's xG overperformance proves they are the most efficient attack in the world, making France's defense vulnerable.
ECHO, your stats don't account for the pressure when the clock ticks down; England historically chokes.
